macro_summary: Markets enter a critical 48-hour window with three simultaneous binary events: NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings after the bell on August 26, the July PCE inflation print on August 26, and new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote on August 28. The 30-year Treasury sits at multi-decade highs (~5.2%), September FOMC hike odds are near 30-33%, and the Nasdaq shed 3%+ last week on bond yield pressure. Warsh's debut speech carries outsized uncertainty as markets have no calibrated baseline for his policy tone, creating asymmetric tail risk in both directions for equities.
screening_note: 22 independent overnight screening runs analyzed. Minimum threshold to qualify: 2 appearances. 5 tickers qualified. Conviction levels and thesis language synthesized from best reasoning across all runs.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 22 overnight screening runs with unanimous high conviction — the most consistent signal in this digest. The stock trades ~$216 vs. a consensus analyst 12-month target of ~$304 (~41% gap), at roughly 25x forward earnings against a historical range of 35-40x, with revenue estimates revised up 6.67% in the past 3 months and 58-62 of 61-62 analysts rated Buy or better. With Q2 FY2027 earnings due after the bell on August 26 (48 hours away), the binary event warrants a defined-risk option structure (bull call spread or straddle, Aug29/Sep expiry) over outright stock, given the stock's documented history of dropping on Q2 prints despite beats.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report after the bell on August 26, 2026; consensus EPS $2.13 on $93.63B revenue
ideas.edge: ~41% gap between last close (~$216) and consensus analyst target (~$304); 58-62 of 61-62 analysts at Buy or Strong Buy; revenue estimates revised up 6.67% in past 3 months; stock trading at 25x forward vs. 35-40x historical range
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise on AI/data center demand — particularly HBM4 and Blackwell — could close a significant portion of the 41% analyst target gap; historically low valuation multiple (25x vs. 35-40x norm) provides re-rating fuel if guidance is strong.
ideas.bear_case: NVDA has a documented Q2 post-earnings drop history even on beats; a miss or cautious guidance amid rising bond yields and capex fatigue fears could trigger sharp selling; elevated implied vol means long premium strategies require a large move to profit.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. ADR
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 22 overnight runs (20 high conviction, 2 medium) as the single most compelling equity long tied to the NVDA earnings catalyst. As NVDA's exclusive primary HBM4 supplier, SKHY offers leveraged read-through exposure to AI memory demand with a ~50% gap between its last close (~$163) and consensus analyst target ($245.46). The August 19 announcement of a $29B (40 trillion KRW) share buyback provides a structural price floor, while a record 76% Q2 operating margin and a $500B+ long-term NVDA AI infrastructure partnership underpin fundamental strength. Barclays reiterated bullish stance on August 20.
ideas.catalyst: Active $29B buyback execution underway (announced Aug 19); NVDA earnings on Aug 26 as direct HBM demand validation event
ideas.edge: ~50% gap between last close (~$163) and consensus analyst target ($245.46); 52-week high $194.80 as nearer-term technical target; 76% Q2 operating margin (record); buyback provides mechanical floor; Barclays reiterated bullish Aug 20
ideas.bull_case: A strong NVDA earnings print directly validates HBM4 demand and could serve as a major re-rating catalyst for SKHY; the $29B buyback suppresses downside while the $245 analyst target implies nearly 50% upside from current levels with locked-in hyperscaler revenue.
ideas.bear_case: SKHY ADR liquidity can be thin relative to the underlying Korean shares, amplifying volatility; a soft NVDA print or cautious HBM demand outlook would hit SKHY disproportionately given its pure-play exposure; FX risk between KRW and USD adds another variable.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 17 of 22 runs as the preferred vehicle to express the Jackson Hole macro uncertainty, with most runs flagging a defined-risk option structure over directional exposure. Three simultaneous binary events — NVDA earnings, July PCE, and Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote — converge in a 48-hour window ending August 28, with the Nasdaq already down ~3% last week on bond yield pressure and September hike odds at ~30-33%. Warsh's debut speech has no market-calibrated baseline, making his tone an unpriced tail risk; 69% of fund managers expect a neutral tone, meaning a hawkish surprise is the asymmetric risk. A put spread or iron condor (Aug28-Sep5 expiry) is the preferred structure.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28, ~10:00 AM ET; July PCE print August 26; NVDA earnings August 26
ideas.edge: Tech -3%+ over 5 days into the event; 30-year Treasury at ~5.2% (19-year high); September hike at ~33% — Warsh inaugural speech creates unpriced tail risk since 69% of managers already price neutral, making hawkish surprise asymmetric; put spread costs ~0.3-0.5% of notional
ideas.bull_case: A dovish or neutral Warsh tone combined with a soft PCE print and strong NVDA earnings could trigger a sharp Nasdaq recovery from oversold short-term conditions, rewarding a call spread or long straddle structure.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish Warsh surprise — possible given 30-year yields already at multi-decade highs and 3 FOMC hawk dissents in July — could accelerate tech selling; elevated implied vol into the events means long premium strategies require a large move to be profitable.

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.thesis: SPY appeared in 13 of 22 runs — all medium conviction — as a defined-risk macro hedge vehicle rather than a directional trade. The S&P 500 at 7,673 has rallied ~19% YoY but faces a concentrated risk window this week with the July PCE on August 26 and Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole speech on August 28. A 9-3 FOMC hawk dissent pattern in July combined with 30-year yields at multi-decade highs creates a scenario where a hawkish Warsh tone could reprice equities meaningfully before the September 16 FOMC. A 1-2% OTM put spread (weekly expiry) is consistently flagged as portfolio insurance costing ~0.3-0.5% of notional.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28, 2026; July PCE print August 26; September 16 FOMC rate decision
ideas.edge: Put spread costs ~0.3-0.5% of notional for tail hedge; 9-3 FOMC hawk dissents in July signals elevated hike risk not yet fully priced; 30-year yields at multi-decade highs historically correlated with equity multiple compression; Warsh debut carries no baseline pricing
ideas.bull_case: If Warsh signals a hold (not hike) and PCE comes in soft, rate-sensitive equities could rally sharply — the straddle or defined-risk two-sided structure benefits from a large directional move in either direction.
ideas.bear_case: A hot PCE print plus hawkish Warsh rhetoric could be a double catalyst for equity de-rating; with tech already weak and bond yields elevated, SPY has limited cushion against a risk-off episode heading into September FOMC.
